name: Sethur
overview: Sethur was a male member of the tribe of Asher and is known as one of the twelve spies sent to explore the land of Canaan. His role as a spy is noted in the book of Numbers, highlighting his participation in this significant mission on behalf of Israel. He is identified specifically as a representative from the tribe of Asher.
namesAndTitles: The name Sethur means 'concealed [by deity],' which reflects a Hebrew proper name with a theologically significant meaning, though it was not given directly by God. This name suggests a divine protection or hiddenness associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Sethur was the father of Michael, establishing a direct familial link mentioned in the same passage that identifies him as a spy. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Sethur's significance lies in his role as one of the twelve spies chosen to scout the Promised Land, a pivotal event in Israel's journey to Canaan. As a representative of the tribe of Asher, he contributed to the collective report that would influence Israel's faith and obedience to God's promises. His inclusion among the spies underscores the importance of tribal representation and the testing of Israel's trust in God's provision.
